oneLine: One screen for everything that wants your attention: your AI coding agents, builds, email, Teams, calendar, bills and packages.
pitch: Anything that needs you turns orange, and you can answer it right there without opening the other app. It runs on your own computer: your passwords and mail never pass through anyone else's server, and nothing is ever sent without your click.

headlines.title: Orange means it needs you
headlines.cool: An agent waiting for an answer, a build that failed, a reply you owe, a bill due, a late package, the chickens to feed: one board, one colour for "you". Everything else stays quiet, so a glance tells you whether you can keep working.
show: Open Now with a few cards on it: one agent waiting, one red build, one email to answer.
Click the waiting agent and answer it; the card leaves and the lamp in the wordmark goes from orange to green.
Before noon: the morning rundown reads the day aloud in one sentence.

headlines.title: Your AI agents live inside it
headlines.cool: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and local models run inside Switchboard, and a Claude session reads like a clean chat: its permission prompts and multiple-choice questions are buttons, messages queue while they work, any file they mention opens with a click, and the bar shows the model, how much context is used and what it has cost so far.
show: Start a Claude session from New session, picking the model and effort.
Claude asks permission: click Yes in the chat. Claude asks a question with choices: tick two and Submit.
Type a second message while it works; it waits and goes in when the agent is free.

headlines.title: Your agents can talk back
headlines.cool: Switchboard is an MCP server, so the agents themselves can read your board: what needs you, how the builds are doing. A stuck agent puts a card on your board instead of sitting silently in a terminal, and one session can hand work to another.
show: Ask an agent "what needs me on Switchboard?" and it answers from the board.
An agent that is blocked adds a Needs-you card; it shows on Now at once.

headlines.title: Work finds the session it is about
headlines.cool: A Teams message or email about a project shows up beside the coding session for that project. One click puts it into what you send the agent, with who sent it and when. A notes page goes in the same way.
show: A teammate's Teams message arrives; it appears under the session list with an orange dot.
Add to message, then Send: the agent gets the message and starts on it.

headlines.title: Reply without opening the other app
headlines.cool: Gmail, any other mail account, Teams, Outlook, Google Voice texts and your team's own end-to-end encrypted chat in one Inbox that reads like a chat app. Reply, archive or snooze from there, and close the dozen tabs: you still see everything.
show: Pick a Teams chat in Inbox; it opens large beside the list.
Write a reply and send it; it shows at once and is confirmed when it has gone.

headlines.title: Every computer, one board
headlines.cool: Sign in on each computer and every session shows on all of them. Open a session running on your desktop from your laptop and it is a chat there too, questions and all. Settings and notes follow you, end-to-end encrypted.
show: On the laptop, open a session that runs on the desktop.
Answer its question from the laptop; the desktop session carries on.

headlines.title: Private, light and yours
headlines.cool: One small local server, one SQLite file and a plain web page, using far less memory than the browser tabs and apps it replaces. No middleman server, no subscription, and nothing sent on your behalf: every email and message goes when you click.
show: Close the browser tabs for mail, Teams, GitHub and the calendar; Switchboard still shows all of it.
Open the System monitor to show how little it uses.
